title: hash maps and frequency tables
concepts: A map associates each key with a value and supports lookup by key
A hash function maps keys to hash codes, while equality decides whether keys match
Distinct keys can collide and a hash table must resolve collisions correctly
Expected constant-time operations rely on distribution and load assumptions; worst-case behavior can be linear
Resizing and rehashing trade occasional linear work for efficient average operations
Frequency maps, complement lookup, grouping, and index maps turn repeated searches into one-pass or near-linear algorithms
Mutable keys and inconsistent equality/hash implementations can invalidate lookup behavior

practiceProblems.name: Two Sum
practiceProblems.statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two values that add to target. Exactly one solution exists and an element cannot be reused.

practiceProblems.name: Group Anagrams
practiceProblems.statement: Group strings that are anagrams of one another. Return the groups in any order.
constraints: strs[i] contains only lowercase English letters.

practiceProblems.name: Top K Frequent Elements
practiceProblems.statement: Return the k most frequent values in nums in any order. The answer is unique.

practiceProblems.name: Longest Consecutive Sequence
practiceProblems.statement: Given an unsorted array of integers, return the length of its longest consecutive-value sequence. The values need not be adjacent in the array and the algorithm must run in O(n) time.

practiceProblems.name: Isomorphic Strings
practiceProblems.statement: Determine whether strings s and t are isomorphic: a consistent character replacement maps s to t while preserving order, and distinct source characters must map to distinct target characters.
constraints: s and t contain valid ASCII characters.

practiceProblems.name: Subarray Sum Equals K
practiceProblems.statement: Return the number of nonempty contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k.
